clue.text: Trespasses with frequency inside old boundary markers

indicators.note: inside tells us the frequency letter goes within the other pieces

parts.note: fences mark the boundaries of fields and gardens
F is the physics abbreviation for frequency

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding line about sins committed repeatedly among the old field fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trespasses' looks like the start of the wordplay, but it is the definition, in the Lord's Prayer sense of sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespasses in the old prayer-book sense are wrongs or sins, which are offences.

clue.text: Keep hitting a sort of ball over

indicators.note: over in a down clue asks for the word to be turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a golf ball is one sort of ball

explanation.surface: A coach tells a player to keep hitting a ball over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is to beat repeatedly, so keeping on hitting is flogging.

clue.text: Dine out on hot food, going up to town

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of dine are put out of order
going up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: grub is slang for food
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone eats out on hot food before travelling up to town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DINE to EDIN; 'going up' turns GRUB into BURG; H ends the word. The definition 'town' is generous, since the answer is Scotland's capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's capital is a city, loosely a town, which the clue's last word names.

clue.text: Oil wheel

definitions.meaning: a pale oil pressed from the beans of the ...-oil plant, used as a laxative
a small swivelling wheel fitted under furniture

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the laxative plant oil and the small swivel wheel under a chair.

clue.text: Thinking lover is strangely shy type

indicators.note: strangely says the following letters appear in an odd, rearranged order

explanation.surface: A thoughtful lover turns out, oddly enough, to be a timid sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges all of THINKING LOVER IS, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring, bashful person is idiomatically named after a modest woodland flower.

clue.text: Stray missile's collected in passing, on board

indicators.note: collected means the missile takes another piece into itself

parts.note: a dart is a small thrown missile; the 's stands for has
e.p. is the chess abbreviation for en passant, a pawn capture made in passing on the board

explanation.surface: A stray missile is picked up by someone passing on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' looks like a ship but points to the chessboard: EP is the chess shorthand for en passant ('in passing').
explanation.definitionFit: To stray from a path is to deviate or leave it, a sense of going off.

clue.text: Exhausted, taken out to be charged with power

indicators.note: to be charged with means one word is filled with another, like a battery loaded with power

parts.note: deleted means taken out or removed
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A flat battery, removed and then charged up again with power.
explanation.walkthrough: The battery imagery of 'charged' and 'power' hides a container: P goes into DELETED.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies that are depleted have been used up, that is, exhausted.

clue.text: Drama not unknown to Republican writer?

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the unknown letter from the drama word

parts.note: a play is a drama
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: A play that is not unknown to a writer from the Republican party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican' suggests US politics, but it refers to the Republic, the dialogue by the Greek philosopher; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian philosopher wrote the dialogue called the Republic, so he is its author.

clue.text: Rascal, one showing contempt for remarkable product

parts.note: a rip is an old word for a rascal or scamp
someone who snorts derisively is a snorter

explanation.surface: A rascal sneers at some remarkable product.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripsnorter is informally something outstandingly good or exciting.

clue.text: Entertainers' journey made feature for newspaper

parts.note: comics are comedians, entertainers
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A comedy troupe's tour gets written up as a newspaper feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers carry cartoon panels telling a short story, a regular feature.

clue.text: Current measures a legislator's assembled

parts.note: an MP, a Member of Parliament, is a legislator; MP's gives MPS

explanation.surface: A lawmaker's assembly measures the current political mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' just says the pieces are put together. The definition is electrical current, not current affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric current is measured in units named after the physicist Ampère.

clue.text: Housework helper's tip given mark of approval

parts.note: in folklore a brownie is a household sprite that does chores at night
a point is a tip, as of a pencil

explanation.surface: A cleaner's helpful tip earns her a mark of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housework helper' suggests a cleaner, but it is the brownie of British folklore, a goblin who does housework while the family sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit earned for currying favour is an idiomatic notional mark of approval.

clue.text: Mafia head's policy about appeal to eminence in Rome

indicators.note: about means the Mafia word goes around another piece

parts.note: a capo is the head of a Mafia family
it is slang for sex appeal
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A mob boss's policy involves appealing to a dignitary in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eminence' suggests a cardinal (His Eminence) but means a hill: the Capitoline is one of the seven hills of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminence is a piece of high ground; this is one of Rome's seven hills.

clue.text: Brace manner, following pressure

indicators.note: following means the manner word comes after the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
an air is a manner or bearing

explanation.surface: Someone braces themselves in a certain manner under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brace' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a brace of pheasants is two.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace means two of something, as in a brace of birds, so a couple.

clue.text: One later taking in a non-professional

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: taking in means one word surrounds another

parts.note: next means later or following
per means a, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: Someone later taking on an amateur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is not a link here: it means PER, as in 'ten pounds a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking skill, a non-professional, is unskilled or amateurish.

clue.text: Latent power of patent oil mixture

indicators.note: mixture says the letters of the phrase are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A patented oil blend carries hidden power.
explanation.definitionFit: Potential is capacity not yet realised, which is latent power.

clue.text: Make reduction, when beautiful girl collects skirt

indicators.note: collects means the girl word gathers another piece inside it

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A pretty girl picks up a skirt whenever prices are cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt' might suggest avoiding something; it is a miniskirt. A DISH is old slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to lessen, which is to make a reduction.

clue.text: Illumination for landing

definitions.meaning: settling on a perch, from to light on, or alight

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both artificial illumination and coming to rest, as a bird lights on a branch.

clue.text: Rain hard to run into when returning

indicators.note: returning says the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to meet is to run into someone

explanation.surface: Heavy rain makes it hard to run into the house when returning.
explanation.definitionFit: When it teems, it pours down, which is raining hard.

clue.text: Durham's opener caught better keeper, they say

indicators.note: caught means one piece is held within the other

parts.note: finer means better

indicators.note: opener means just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Durham opening batsman is caught by the better wicketkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface (Durham is an English cricket county) misleads; the definition plays on the saying 'finders keepers', so a finder is a keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The playground saying grants ownership to whoever discovers a lost thing, so the discoverer keeps it.

clue.text: Dealing with large numbers in tedious disagreement

parts.note: long can mean tedious, as in a long day
division is disagreement within a group

explanation.surface: A dull dispute drags on in a big organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: This written arithmetic method divides by multi-digit numbers, step by step on paper.

clue.text: Good philosopher makes one merrier

parts.note: A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A good philosopher cheers people up.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense the word means more cheerful or jolly, that is, merrier.

clue.text: Another Aphrodite — some goddess!

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the sight of yet another Aphrodite.
explanation.walkthrough: Aphrodite primes a goddess, which is right, but the answer is a different goddess, Zeus's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: She was queen of the Greek gods, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: Two such white boys, and a girl

definitions.meaning: the folk song Green Grow the Rushes, O has 'Two, two
a girl's name, from the flower

explanation.surface: A count of two pale boys and one girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading relies on the English folk song Green Grow the Rushes, O, whose second verse sings of the 'lily-white boys'.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower name completes the song's lily-white phrase and is also a girl's name.

clue.text: Silly boy — devil is out to seize him

indicators.note: to seize means the jumbled letters grab hold of the boy word
out signals the letters of devil is are knocked out of order

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A foolish boy, and the devil is out to grab him.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a tempted boy; 'out' and 'to seize' are the anagram and container signals, the jumbled letters closing round the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwise or foolish is badly thought out, hence silly.

clue.text: Home ground is on height

indicators.note: is on in an across clue means the ground word sits after the height letter

parts.note: earth is ground or soil

explanation.surface: A homestead's grounds lie up on high land.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside stands for the home, as in hearth and home.

clue.text: Apprentice has to rely on European

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner or apprentice
to lean on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A trainee has to depend on a colleague from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Tyrol, an Alpine region of Austria and Italy, is a European.
